basis: Decompile: mute path writes property 0x4001 = 3; unmute path writes 0x4001 = 0 then 0x4000 = 0x3F. In the Si47xx property map 0x4001 is RX_HARD_MUTE (bit0 right, bit1 left, so 3 = both) and 0x4000 is RX_VOLUME (0x3F = maximum)

basis: Decompile: reads up to 32 bytes from the serial flash via SPIFLASH_ReadBytes, then scans LSB-first for the first set bit and returns its bit index, or 0xFF when none is set

basis: Called by the channel-save path as (channel_number, record_pointer, name_pointer), with the channel number computed as base + zone * 0x40

notes: The zone * 0x40 term independently confirms 64 channels per zone, matching the 0x800 zone / 0x20 record arithmetic in CHANNEL_LoadToSlot.

basis: Decompile: gathers 0x20 bytes from the settings struct at 0x2000A7C0 and 0x25 from 0x2000A7E0 into one 0x60 buffer, CRC16s 0x5E bytes of it, finds a slot via STORAGE_FindFirstSetBit(0x9000, 6), then compares the stored CRC at slot*0x60 + 0x906E before deciding whether to rewrite
purpose: Writes the settings block to flash, skipping the write when the CRC already matches.
notes: This is a wear-levelling scheme: a 6-byte allocation bitmap at flash 0x9000 (48 slots), 0x60-byte records, the CRC stored at record offset 0x6E, and a slot cap of 0x29 (41). Explains the 0x9000 address noted vaguely in the original catalogue for Flash_ReadWrite_Block. Read this before writing settings by hand.

basis: Format strings "153-279", "520-1710", " 2.3-30", " 64-108", "0.15-30" - the standard LW, MW, SW and FM broadcast band edges in kHz and MHz

notes: These are exactly the bands an Si4732 covers: LW 153-279 kHz, MW 520-1710 kHz, SW 2.3-30 MHz, FM 64-108 MHz. Only visible after the base was corrected.

purpose: Turns the green status LED on or off.

Argument 0 = off, 1 = on, 2 = turn on only if currently off. Their struct sits at 0x200001DE in firmware V0.27 vs 0x200001DA in the V0.18 image analysed here - a 4-byte shift - but the +2/+3 field offsets match exactly.

purpose: Shows the bilingual "Save OK" confirmation popup.

Both numbers were artefacts of the old project mis-bounding functions: correctly analysed it is 160 bytes with 5 callers. The string at 0x080182EC is " Save OK" and 0x080182F8 is GB2312 "保存". notes: SCANQT is presumably scan-with-tone-qualify; unconfirmed.

basis: Decompile: returns open when the squelch setting byte is zero, otherwise returns bit 1 of register 0x0C. RT-890 BK4819_CheckSquelchLink is the same test on the same register and bit
purpose: Reports whether the squelch is currently open.
notes: The shift test (value << 0x1E < 0) is bit 1. Also pins SRAM 0x2000A7C0[0] as the squelch setting, the 890 gSettings.Squelch. The 890 additionally bypasses on monitor mode; the 950 guard here is a single byte.

basis: Decompile cross-referenced against the HW_PROBED silkscreen names in rt950-scratch/include/rt950_pinmap.h: PE12=U3R, PE13=U6R, PE14=SW3T, PE7=U3T, PB0=V3R, PB1=V3T. Each call drives exactly one line high and clears the competing ones
purpose: Selects the RF front-end path for a band, in either receive or transmit.
notes: *** CORRECTION *** The existing catalogue calls this PTT_Relay_Select and pinout.md reads PE13/PE12/PE14/PE7 as primary PTT / external PTT / PA gate / mic toggle. It is an antenna-path switch matrix. mode 1 = pick RX path (band 1,3 -> U3R; band 4 -> U6R; else V3R), mode 2 = pick TX path (band 0,2 -> V3T; band 1,3 -> U3T; band 4 -> SW3T), mode 3 = all RX off, mode 0 = everything off. Note Hertzz58 annotates these pins ACTIVE LOW, but the code drives the SELECTED line high and the others low - active low would mean it disables the path it is selecting, so active high is the correct reading and that annotation looks wrong. Hertzz58 also carries PTT_PRIMARY/PTT_EXTERNAL aliases that it marks as inherited JKI757 labels, i.e. the same mistake imported.

basis: Decompile: writes registers 0x70, 0x72, 0x58, 0x5C, 0x5D in the same order as RT-890 BK4819_EnableFFSK1200, and disables by writing 0x70=0 then 0x58=0 exactly as the 890 does. 0x5C=0x5665 and 0x5D=0x0F00 are bit-identical to the 890
purpose: Enables or disables the FFSK data modem.
notes: The three rate-dependent constants differ from the 890 (0x70=0x00AC vs 0x00E0, 0x72=0x60CA vs 0x3065, 0x58=0x00C9 vs 0x37C3), which is what a different FFSK bit rate looks like - the 890 path is explicitly 1200 baud, so the 950 is probably not. Also writes 0x59/0x3F, which the 890 does in its FSK reset path. NOTE (later evidence): a second routine at 0x0801BBE4 writes 0x72=0x3065, which is the 890 1200-baud constant exactly, so THAT one is the 1200-baud path and this one is a different rate. Treat the rate labelling of the two as unresolved.

basis: Decompile: writes register 0x51 as (gain & 0x7F) | 0x9000, the exact idiom of RT-890 BK4819_WriteRegister(0x51, CtcssTxGain | 0x9000); writes 0x51=0 to disable, plus 0x07=0x471 and a masked update of 0x52
purpose: Enables CTCSS transmission and applies the per-band TX gain.
notes: Gain is read from the band-calibration block at SRAM 0x2000011E, the same source the 890 calls gFrequencyBandInfo.CtcssTxGainNarrow/Wide.

basis: Called from state 0 of RADIO_RunStateMachine with ten arguments drawn from the channel record and settings (frequency, sub-audible codes, power, bandwidth flags), immediately before the machine advances to receive
purpose: Programs the transceiver for the current channel.
notes: The single point where a channel becomes live RF state. Two call sites differ only in whether the config comes from an explicit block or a pointer at +0x1C.

basis: Decompile: forwards to BK4829_SetAfModeAndGain with AF mode 1 when muting and 0 otherwise
purpose: Mutes or unmutes the receiver audio path.
notes: 7 callers, all around state transitions.

basis: Clears a 0x54-byte struct at SRAM 0x2000A2E0 and sets the byte at 0x20000B2C to 0xFF; 26 callers
purpose: Resets an edit/scratch record.
notes: Shape-based only. 0x54 bytes is a plausible channel or menu-edit record; the 0xFF sentinel suggests 'no selection'.

basis: Decompile: reloads the countdown at UI-state +0x2E with settings byte 0x2000A7C0[0x10] multiplied by 50
purpose: Restarts the menu/display inactivity timeout.
notes: Implies SRAM 0x2000A7C0+0x10 is the user-set timeout, in units of 50 ticks. 11 callers.

basis: Decompile: drives GPIOC bit 0x0010 (PC4) high or low, either directly from its second argument or from radio-state conditions when the first argument is zero
purpose: Drives the hardware audio mute line.
notes: PC4 is not in the Hertzz58 pinmap, so the pin function is inferred from context: it is toggled around transmit and receive transitions alongside the BK4829 mute. Needs a scope to confirm.

basis: Read-modify-write of BK4829 register 0x7D, replacing the low bits with a value from SRAM 0x2000011E. RT-890 analog: BK4819_SetMicSensitivityTuning() writes 0xE940 | Tuning to the same register 0x7D
purpose: Applies the per-band microphone sensitivity trim.
notes: The 950 preserves the high bits rather than rewriting the whole 0xE940 constant, but the register and the field are the same as the 890.

basis: Decompile: writes the low half of the frequency to register 0x38 and the high half to 0x39 - the same pair RT-890 BK4819_SetFrequency uses - then selects the channel filter via 0x43
purpose: Tunes the synthesiser and applies the matching filter bandwidth.
notes: Wide constant 0x43=0x3028 is bit-identical to the 890; the narrow constant differs (0x4008 here vs 0x4048 in the 890), which is a genuine per-model difference worth noting before copying filter settings across.

basis: RT-890 analog: I2C_Send() in driver/bk4819.c, called identically with (0x80|reg) for reads
purpose: Bit-bangs one byte to a BK4829 over the 3-wire bus.
notes: Radtel/DualTachyon call this bus 'I2C' in the 890 even though it is a 3-wire SPI variant.

basis: Decompile: toggles bit 0 of BK4829 register 0x31 and writes three constant sets to 0x42/0x2A/0x2B, selected by a mode argument (6, 8, or default)
purpose: Switches the transceiver between modulation/filter profiles.
notes: RT-890 shows register 0x31 as a bit-field (bit1 scramble, bit2 VOX, bit3 compander); bit 0 is not used by the 890 so its meaning here is unconfirmed. Constants: mode 6 -> 0x42=0x6F5C, 0x2A=0x7434, 0x2B=0x0500; default -> 0x42=0x6B5A, 0x2A=0x7400.

basis: Decompile: writes 0x37=0x9F1F, drops the transceiver, calls BK4829_SetFrequency, writes 0x51=0x0300, then returns to RX
purpose: Retunes and restarts the receiver with CSS auto-bandwidth disabled.
notes: The 890 writes 0x37=0x1F0F in BK4819_EnableRX; the 0x9F1F here sets an additional high bit, so the power-up sequencing differs slightly between models.

basis: Decompile: writes 0x72=0x3065 - bit-identical to RT-890 BK4819_EnableFFSK1200 - plus 0x58, 0x70, 0x5D, 0x59, sync words 0x5A/0x5B, length 0x5C and 0x3F
purpose: Configures the FSK modem for the 1200-baud FFSK profile.
notes: The matching 0x72 constant is what distinguishes this from the other FFSK setup at 0x0801AC8C. Sync words 0x5A=0xFB72 / 0x5B=0x4099 are specific to this profile.

basis: Decompile: writes 0x3F=0 and 0x59=0x0028, identical to RT-890 BK4819_ResetFSK, then 0x70=0 and 0x58=0, identical to the 890 FFSK disable path
purpose: Returns the FSK block to idle.
notes: Effectively the 890 ResetFSK and EnableFFSK1200(false) merged into one routine. Where the 890 finishes with 0x30=0 (power off) the 950 leaves the transceiver state alone.

basis: Decompile: configures 0x3F/0x59, loads sync words into 0x5A/0x5B, sets length via 0x5C, pushes seven halfwords into the 0x5F FIFO, then writes 0x59=0x0828 to start and polls for completion with a timeout
purpose: Transmits one FSK/FFSK data frame.
notes: Register roles follow the BK4819 FSK block (0x5A/0x5B sync, 0x5F FIFO, 0x59 control). The 7-halfword payload matches the 14-byte block copied in from the table at 0x0801BFD4.

basis: Structure matches RT-890 BK4819_ReadRegister exactly: assert CS, send 0x80|reg, flip SDA to input, clock in 16 bits, release CS. CS pin = PE15 = Hertzz58 BK4829_SEN2_PIN
purpose: Reads a 16-bit register from BK4829 #2.
notes: *** CORRECTION *** The existing catalogue calls this Band_Relay_ShiftIn and pinout.md describes PE15/PE10/PE11 as an 'RF filter relay shift interface'. It is the BK4829 control bus: PE15=SEN2, PE10=SCK, PE11=SDA.

basis: Decompile: writes BK4829 register 0x30 through the ops table, with constants bit-identical to the RT-890: 0x0200 priming, 0xBFF1 = RX, 0xC1FE = TX with mic, 0xC3FA = TX without mic, 0x0000 = off
purpose: Puts the transceiver into receive, transmit or off.
notes: The strongest Rosetta match found so far - the magic values match RT-890 BK4819_EnableRX/EnableTX exactly (driver/bk4819.c lines 285-286, 517-527). Argument: 1 = RX, 2 = TX with mic, 3/4 = the remaining cases. Calls via *(0x20000B90), which re-confirms the ops table.

basis: Decompile: transceiver off, write 0x51=0x0300, transceiver back to RX. RT-890 BK4819_DisableAutoCssBW writes the identical 0x51=0x0300 then calls BK4819_EnableRX
purpose: Disables the automatic CSS bandwidth adjustment.
notes: The 950 brackets the write with explicit state changes where the 890 uses a delay plus EnableRX; the register write is bit-identical.

basis: Decompile: writes register 0x47 from a 16-entry mode table OR 0x6042, then register 0x48 as (gain & 0x3F) << 4 | 0xB00F. RT-890 BK4819_SetAF writes 0x47 and BK4819_SetAfGain writes 0x48, taking the gain from gFrequencyBandInfo.RX_DAC_GainNarrow/Wide exactly as this does
purpose: Selects the AF output mode and applies the per-band receive gain.
notes: Pins two more calibration fields: 0x2000011E[3] = RX DAC gain wide, [4] = narrow, selected by the same narrow/wide flag at ops+0x21 that BK4829_SetFrequency uses to pick the filter. Modes 3 and 0xF1 skip the gain write (mute paths).

basis: Decompile: writes the frequency to 0x38/0x39, then reads 0x30, writes 0x30=0 and restores it
purpose: Retunes and bounces the PLL/power register so the synthesiser relocks.
notes: Distinct from BK4829_SetFrequency, which also selects the filter but does not restart the PLL. Likely the scan-step path.

basis: Decompile: read-modify-write of register 0x31 bit 1 plus a write to 0x71 - exactly the register pair and bit RT-890 BK4819_EnableScramble uses
purpose: Enables voice inversion scrambling at a selected level.
notes: The 890 computes 0x71 arithmetically (0x68DC | level*1032); the 950 instead indexes a 9-entry table at 0x0801C520 and clamps the level to 9. Guarded by a frequency check before it will engage.

basis: Decompile: writes register 0x71 as (tone * 0xFC0FC) / 10000. RT-890 BK4819_SetToneFrequency writes the same register as (Tone * 103) / 10
purpose: Programs the tone generator frequency.
notes: Same register and the same physical scale factor: the 890 uses 10.3 counts per Hz, the 950 uses 103.2188 per 10 units - i.e. the 950 takes its tone argument in tenths of a hertz, giving 10x finer resolution with a more precise constant. Worth knowing before copying tone tables across models.

basis: Decompile: clears the tone generator (SetToneFrequency(0), 0x70=0), selects RX or TX state from a helper, then re-applies AF mode/gain and the scramble setting
purpose: Returns the receiver to normal audio after a tone or data burst.
notes: Reads the scramble level from ops+0x26. The RX/TX choice comes from FUN_0801BDC4, which is the remaining unnamed predicate in this path.

basis: Identical body to FUN_8001c04c but CS = PE8 = Hertzz58 BK4829_SEN1_PIN
purpose: Reads a 16-bit register from BK4829 #1.
notes: *** CORRECTION *** Same as above. Confirms two BK4829s share SCK/SDA and differ only in chip select.

basis: Calls DISPLAY_SetPanelEnable(0), AUDIO_SetPathOwner(6) (release owner 2), and clears three flags in the 0x2000A334 state struct
purpose: Tears down the active mode and returns to idle.
notes: Shape-based; the call sequence is a clean shutdown but the exact scope is unconfirmed.

basis: Existing entry confirmed: emits 0x2A then 0x2B, each with start and end-1
purpose: Defines the drawing rectangle.
notes: Args are (x0, x_end_exclusive, y0, y_end_exclusive); the function subtracts 1 before sending.

basis: Literal pool reaches the string 'APRS'
purpose: APRS-related feature entry point.
notes: Newly surfaced; needs decomposition.

basis: Same string set as UI_DrawToneFieldNarrow with wider padding
purpose: Draws a sub-audible tone field in the wide layout.

basis: RT-890 analog: SPEAKER_TurnOn/TurnOff(Owner). The 890 uses an owner bitmask; the 950 uses a 6-byte owner flag array at g_200001E2
purpose: Reference-counted enable for the audio output path.
notes: Odd param = claim owner, even = release; default case releases all and disables. Drives PE4 and PB8 high to enable, plus PC9. 25 callers.

basis: Decompile: loads 4 entries from the table at 0x080309A8 and 5 from 0x080309B8, formats each with lib_sprintf and draws them at y=0x27 and y=0x52
purpose: Draws the squelch-multiplier and channel-spacing menu values.
notes: The two tables are the x16/x32/x64/x128 and 6.25k/8.33k/12.5k/20.0k/25.0k string lists. Only readable at all because of the 0x2C00 image correction.

basis: Decompile: three-entry string table at 0x080309CC, indexed by param % 2, drawn at x=0xCF y=0x26
purpose: Draws a short mode label in the top-right field.
notes: Index is taken modulo 2 although the table holds three entries; the third may be unused or reached elsewhere.

basis: Decompile: fills the fixed window x 0x2A..0xCC, y 0x31..0x4B, draws one argument through a text helper at that origin, then flushes
purpose: Redraws a fixed titled field near the top of the screen.
notes: Shape-based: the window is hard-coded, so this is one specific screen region, but which field it is has not been established.

basis: Polled in a loop after page program until it returns zero
purpose: Reads the status register and returns the WIP/busy bit.
notes: Standard SPI NOR RDSR (0x05) poll.

basis: Existing catalog entry
purpose: Block erase (32 KiB).
notes: Retained.

basis: Existing catalog entry
purpose: Block erase (64 KiB).
notes: Retained.

basis: Existing catalog entry (Software_SPI_FlashErase4K), consistent with the SPI NOR command set
purpose: Sector erase.
notes: Retained; renamed for consistency with SPIFLASH_ReadBytes.

basis: Decompile: asserts PB12, sends command 0x03 plus a 24-bit big-endian address, then streams bytes in
purpose: Reads a byte range from the external SPI NOR flash.
notes: *** CORRECTION *** pinout.md attributes PB12 to 'BK4829 #1 on hardware SPI1'. Command 0x03 is SPI NOR READ, and Hertzz58 hardware-verified PB12 as FLASH_CS on SPI2. No SPI1 register access appears anywhere in the image.

basis: Innermost bit-bang byte routine used by every SPI NOR command sequence
purpose: Shifts one byte out to the serial flash.
notes: Previously catalogued as Software_SPI_Write_Byte.

basis: Decompile: CS low on PB12, command 0x02 + 24-bit address, data bytes, CS high, then polls busy with a 10000-iteration timeout
purpose: Programs up to one 256-byte page of the serial flash.
notes: 0x02 is SPI NOR PAGE PROGRAM. Confirms PB12 = flash CS (see SPIFLASH_ReadBytes).

basis: Decompile: computes 0x100 - (addr & 0xff) and splits the transfer on 256-byte boundaries, calling SPIFLASH_PageProgram per chunk
purpose: Page-boundary-aware write of an arbitrary byte range.
notes: This is the function to use when patching stored settings; writing across a page boundary directly would wrap within the page.

basis: Called immediately before every program/erase sequence, the standard place for SPI NOR WREN (0x06)
purpose: Issues WRITE ENABLE before a program or erase.
notes: Command byte not re-read in this pass; position in the sequence is the evidence.

basis: Decompile: switch on the state byte at SRAM 0x2000A334[4] with at least nine cases; case 1 arms the TX path via RF_SelectPath(band, 2), loads a timeout from settings[5] and advances the state
purpose: One pass of the main receive/transmit state machine.
notes: The core sequencer - the highest-value function to finish decomposing. Touches 12 distinct settings bytes, more than any other function. settings[5] is scaled by 300 into a tick countdown, which is the shape of a TX time-out timer.

basis: Decompile: if the string is at least as long as the field, copy field-width bytes; otherwise space-fill the field (memset value 0x20) and copy the string at offset (width - length) / 2
purpose: Copies a string centred within a fixed-width field.
notes: The (width - len) >> 1 offset is unambiguous centring. Used by the UI to lay out labels in fixed cells.

basis: The shared bail-out target of states 3 and 8: calls two teardown helpers, sets a 0x28 timer, and clears the mode byte when SYS_GetModeFlag is non-zero
purpose: Abandons the current transmit sequence and returns to receive.

basis: Decompile: gated on the voice-prompt enable byte settings[7]; when the language byte settings[8] is not 1 it adds 0x3C to the prompt index before queueing it at 0x200106FC
purpose: Queues a numbered voice prompt in the selected language.
notes: The +0x3C language offset means the voice bank holds 60 prompts per language laid out back to back - which fits the tagged-record region described in FINDINGS.md as a probable voice bank.

basis: Decompile: if SRAM 0x2000A7C0[7] is set and the first argument is non-zero, plays a voice prompt; otherwise falls back to a plain beep
purpose: Plays a voice prompt when enabled, else a beep.
notes: SRAM 0x2000A7C0[7] is the voice-prompt enable setting.

basis: Called twice per coordinate by LCD_SetAddressWindow
purpose: Writes a 16-bit value as two data bytes, MSB first.
notes: Not previously catalogued.

basis: Decompile: writes ms+1 into the counter at SRAM 0x2000A26C then spins calling the task pump until it reaches zero
purpose: Cooperative blocking delay that keeps background tasks running.
notes: Unlike DELAY_WaitMS this does not stall the radio; use it for UI dwell times. 10 callers.

basis: Literal pool reaches 'VX-8'
purpose: Formats a Yaesu VX-8 style APRS message or identifies that device type.
notes: Newly surfaced; speculative.

basis: Its only identified caller builds a 6-byte SI4732 SET_PROPERTY frame and passes it here; the body is a start / delay / transfer sequence over the bit-banged bus
purpose: Sends a command frame to the SI4732 broadcast receiver.
notes: *** CORRECTS MY OWN EARLIER GUESS *** I named this LCD_SendInitSequence purely from its address neighbourhood (0x08026xxx sits near the LCD code). The caller evidence says SI4732. Hertzz58 puts the SI4732 on bit-banged I2C at PB6/PB7.

basis: Decompile: builds the byte sequence 0x12, 0x00, prop_hi, prop_lo, val_hi, val_lo in a 6-byte buffer at SRAM 0x2000019E and sends it. That is exactly the Si47xx SET_PROPERTY command frame
purpose: Sets an SI4732 property.
notes: Command 0x12 with a zero second byte and two big-endian 16-bit fields is the documented Si47xx SET_PROPERTY layout, which makes this identification essentially certain despite the surrounding code being unnamed. Also gives SRAM 0x2000019E as the SI4732 command buffer.

basis: Decompile: LCD_SetWindow then pushes one constant colour for w*h pixels
purpose: Fills a rectangle with a solid colour.
notes: Args (y, x, w, h, colour). The constant-colour counterpart to LCD_DrawImage.

basis: Existing entry confirmed by disassembly; corrected polarity
purpose: Emits one command byte on the 8080 bus.
notes: Sequence with corrected polarity: CS(PD1) LOW = assert, D/C(PD3) LOW = command, WR(PD0) LOW then HIGH latches. Corroborated by Hertzz58 LCD_WR/CS/DC pin notes.

basis: Existing entry; same handshake as LCD_WriteCommand with D/C high
purpose: Emits one data byte on the 8080 bus.

basis: Decompile: nested loop over a 1-bit-per-pixel source, 8-row banding, foreground/background colour args
purpose: Blits a monochrome glyph or icon with selectable colours.
notes: Args: (x, y, h, w, src, bg_colour, fg_colour). Clamps to 240 rows. RT-890 analog: FONT_Draw / gfx helpers.

basis: Decompile: LCD_SetWindow then row-major loop pushing byte-swapped RGB565 pairs from a source buffer
purpose: Blits a full-colour image/sprite to the panel.
notes: Args (y, x, w, h, src). 23 callers. Companion to LCD_DrawBitmap1bpp, which handles the 1-bpp case.

basis: Body is exactly LCD_WriteCommand(0x2C)
purpose: Issues MIPI-DCS RAMWR to begin pixel streaming.
notes: Not previously catalogued.

basis: As above
purpose: Compiler soft-float double-precision routine.
notes: Not firmware logic. This block (0x08027C00-0x08029600) is almost entirely compiler runtime.

basis: Same signature as the other double helpers: 64-bit exponent masking, FPSCR reference, inline literal pool reached through lr
purpose: Compiler soft-float double-precision routine.
notes: Not firmware logic.

basis: Decompile: extracts the sign, negates to absolute value, normalises with a leading-zero count, then assembles exponent (0x41D - lz) << 20 and a mantissa from the shifted value. 0x41D = 1053 = the double bias 1023 + 30, which is exactly the int-to-double normalisation constant
purpose: Converts a signed 32-bit integer to double.
notes: Precise identification of one of the soft-float helpers previously catalogued only generically. ARM EABI name __aeabi_i2d.

basis: Identical to lib_aeabi_i2d with the sign extraction removed
purpose: Converts an unsigned 32-bit integer to double.
notes: ARM EABI name __aeabi_ui2d.

basis: Manipulates the 0xFFE00000 exponent field of 64-bit values, references FPSCR, and reads its own inline constant pool via (lr + 2) & ~3 - the signature of an __aeabi double-precision helper
purpose: Compiler soft-float double-precision routine.
notes: Not firmware logic; listed so a reader does not spend time on it. Exact operation (add/mul/div) not pinned down.

basis: Same shape as lib_softfloat_double_a: double exponent masking, FPSCR reference, inline literal pool via lr
purpose: Compiler soft-float double-precision routine.
notes: As above.
